belongs_to: Figure it out Q1 (a) 36°, 72°: 'Process for (a) is given' - triangle ABC with line XY drawn through A parallel to BC (alternate angles argument)
description: Triangle ABC with a straight line XY through the top vertex A. Triangle: B at the bottom left, C at the bottom right, side BC horizontal and the longest-looking base; A at the top, placed to the right of the middle of BC (nearer C than B), so AB is a long slanting side rising to the right and AC a short steep side sloping down to the right. Three sides AB, AC, BC drawn as plain solid lines. Line XY: a horizontal straight line through A, parallel to BC, with an arrowhead at BOTH ends (left end points left, right end points right); A lies on this line; the line spans from a little right of the vertical through B (left end about 1/6 of BC to the right of B) to a little beyond the vertical through C (right end about 1/6 of BC past C); A is about 4/5 of the way along BC from B. Labels: X above the left end of the line, A above the vertex A on the line, Y above the right end; B below the left vertex, C below the right vertex. Angle marks: at B a single small arc between BC and BA with the label '36°' written inside the triangle just to the right of the arc; at C a single larger arc between CB and CA with the label '72°' written inside the triangle just to the left of the arc. No angle is marked at A and no angle is marked at X or Y. Shape is drawn to scale: angle B = 36°, angle C = 72° (so angle A = 72°, not shown). No shading, no other marks. The printed answer text under it (not part of the figure) gives ∠XAB = ∠B = 36°, ∠YAC = ∠C = 72° (alternate angles), ∠XAB + ∠BAC + ∠YAC = 180°, so ∠BAC = 72°.

belongs_to: Figure it out Q3: 'Here is a triangle in which we know ∠B = ∠C and ∠A = 50°. Can you find ∠B and ∠C?'
description: An isosceles-looking triangle ABC standing on its base: A at the top apex, B at the bottom left, C at the bottom right, BC horizontal at the bottom, AB and AC the two equal slanting sides (apex roughly above the middle of BC; the triangle is taller than it is wide, drawn to scale with ∠A = 50° and ∠B = ∠C = 65°). Three plain solid sides. Labels: A above the apex, B just left of the bottom-left vertex, C just right of the bottom-right vertex. Angle marks: at A a single small arc across the apex with the label '50°' written inside the triangle just below the arc; at B a single small arc between BC and BA and at C a single small arc between CB and CA, both with NO number (the two same-style single arcs show that ∠B = ∠C, as the question states in words). No other marks, no shading. The unknown base angles are not given a value or a letter on the figure. The printed answer (text only, no picture) is ∠B = ∠C = 65°.
